Messages.Author: Charles Richard Robb
Messages.Body:
Say I have Ozmo in the uncontrolle4d region and someone has him in the controlled region. Could I malk Dem. Ozmo from the other guy and then bring him out
at the end of my turn, contesting him with my self and then give up the
'stolen' Ozmo, thus gaining control of my own Ozmo?
.

Messages.Author: L. Scott Johnson
Messages.Body:
In article <3s9l56$r...@NNTP.MsState.Edu>,

Charles Richard Robb <cr...@Ra.MsState.Edu> wrote:
>Say I have Ozmo in the uncontrolle4d region and someone has him in the controlled region. Could I malk Dem. Ozmo from the other guy and then bring him out
>at the end of my turn, contesting him with my self and then give up the
>'stolen' Ozmo, thus gaining control of my own Ozmo?

No, because you no longer control the stolen Ozmo after the start of
you untap and you can't yield him until after the start of your untap.
(card text: "you control ... until your next untap.")

Messages.Author: James R. McClure Jr.
Messages.Body:
cr...@Ra.MsState.Edu (Charles Richard Robb) wrote:
>Say I have Ozmo in the uncontrolle4d region and someone has him in the controlled
>region. Could I malk Dem. Ozmo from the other guy and then bring him out
>at the end of my turn, contesting him with my self and then give up the
>'stolen' Ozmo, thus gaining control of my own Ozmo?

Peace Charles,

No, you can't yield a contested card until the first Untap Phase after the contesting
card came into play. Since the MD'd vamp will return to its owner as the very first
thing you do in your turn (before you untap), you could not yield the MD'd vamp.

Nil carborundum illigitimi,
